transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-18
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (CTO, NexaHealth), Jasmine Lee (Data Eng), Ravi Gupta (ML Eng)

Summary: quick onboarding check, verify access and peering status, review last week's benchmark numbers (p99 spikes at long sequences), plan tuning / quantization and define next steps.

[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check-in — is this still a good time?
[00:08] Carlos: Yep, good to go. we have 45, right?
[00:11] Ethan: Yup, 45 minutes. I'll hand it over to Priya to pull up the benchmark notes.
[00:18] Priya: cool, thanks. so we ran the dedicated pool tests last week, ran baseline on the 7B open model and a redwood-verified variant. overall throughput looks good but we saw p99 spikes around 2.5k sequence lengths, especially when cache miss rate was high.
[00:34] Ravi: When you say p99 spikes, what's the magnitude? like double? triple? 
[00:39] Priya: roughly 2.5x compared to p50. p50 stayed ~120ms per token, p99 climbed to ~320ms in those scenarios. the interesting bit is when the KV cache can't be reused due to unique prefixes, latency jumps.
[00:55] Jasmine: that's consistent with our internal tests too, we get intermittent high tail latency when some of our queries are long-context retrievals, memory-heavy.
[01:05] Ethan: got it. two threads here: networking / access so we can run our tests from Nexa's VPC and the tuning side to reduce those tails. on networking, Jasmine where are we with the peering request?
[01:15] Jasmine: I sent the initial peering CIDR yesterday, still waiting on infra team for the firewall rules. I can push the ticket, but we'll need Redwood's recommended ports and maybe a diagram for the peering flow.
[01:26] Priya: perfect — we'll share a minimal diagram. Redwood requires egress on ports 443 and 9000 for metrics and model artifact pulls; for private we'll include KMS endpoints. we'll include a sample security group and route table snippet. sorry — might've said 9k, should be 9000.
[01:40] Carlos: for compliance we'll need the network diagram plus SOC2 doc. can you include that in the same email?
[01:46] Ethan: absolutely, I'll attach the SOC2 summary and the network diagram, and KMS integration notes.
[01:51] Ravi: on the benchmarking — can you share the raw stats? averages, percentiles and batch sizes?
[01:56] Priya: yes, we have a spreadsheet. i trimmed it to p50/p90/p99 across batch sizes 1,4,8,16 and seq lengths 512,1024,2048. i'll send the trimmed version after the call. there was one anomalous run where the worker restarted and spiked, i'll flag those rows.
[02:16] Jasmine: great. when you say worker restarted, is that a runtime flake or something in the test harness?
[02:21] Priya: looked like a runtime OOM on one host — we were running a burst path with slightly higher mem use and the worker autoscaler bounced one node. we have logs and a note in the sheet.
[02:33] Ravi: ok, that could explain the p99 outlier. can we re-run that exact config with kv cache warm and then with cold to see delta?
[02:41] Priya: yes, plan is to run a cold vs warm cache comparison — i'll add cold/warm columns in the spreadsheet.
[02:47] Ethan: timeline wise, if Jasmine can get peering set up by end of week we can run those tests early next week and then convene for a tuning session mid next week. does that work for you all?
[02:58] Jasmine: sounds good, i can escalate to infra.
[03:02] Carlos: also need to verify IAM access — do you need a service account from us or will you use a cross-account role?
[03:08] Priya: for the pilot we prefer a test IAM user with limited privileges, or a cross-account role is fine. we'll provide an exportable policy; ideally we get a dedicated test principal so logs link to Nexa's account.
[03:20] Jasmine: i'll share credentials in the secure channel. we'll rotate after the POC.
[03:24] Ravi: on model variants — what's the plan for quantization? we tried 4-bit on our side and saw slight quality degradation.
[03:31] Priya: right — our suggestion is to test a few quant profiles: 8-bit for baseline latency improvement, then 4-bit with mixed quant to preserve key layers. we'll run evals on your prompt set and report quality delta.
[03:45] Ravi: ok please include an automated eval plan. we have about 20 canonical prompts.
[03:49] Priya: perfect, please send them after the call. we'll add them to the eval harness and include Rouge-like and response-quality checks, plus a token-level cost comparison.
[03:58] Ethan: note for pricing — we can propose a small Dedicated burst allowance for the pilot to keep costs predictable. i'll follow up with a short commercial note.
[04:06] Carlos: thanks. one security question — how is logs retention handled? we need audit logs and to make sure no PII is retained longer than our policy.
[04:14] Ethan: by default logs are retained for 30 days on the pilot, but we can configure retention and disable request/response logging for certain routes. we support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[04:26] Jasmine: could we have a configuration where chat-level content is not stored but request metadata is kept?
[04:31] Priya: yes, that's doable — we have a redact/skip logging flag per route. we'll include config examples.
[04:36] Ravi: any known gotchas for on-prem vs VPC?
[04:40] Priya: on-prem requires an extra packaging step and offline artifact transfer; VPC peering is much faster to stand up. for on-prem we'd need a maintenance window for artifact install.
[04:51] Ethan: ok, let's recap next steps real quick. Priya will share the trimmed benchmark spreadsheet and flag anomalies; Ethan will send SOC2 and network diagram; Jasmine will push peering and provide IAM/test account; Raven — sorry Ravi, you'll send the prompt set.
[05:05] Ravi: yep, sending prompts today.
[05:08] Jasmine: i'll try to have peering by Thursday.
[05:11] Priya: we'll schedule the tuning session for next Tuesday afternoon, propose 90 minutes.
[05:16] Ethan: sounds good. Any other questions?
[05:19] Carlos: no, good call. appreciate the clarity.
[05:22] Ethan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the deck and the attachments.

Auto-generated Notes/Action Items: see action_items above.
